title: Latent market cartography for model sourcing and prospect prioritizer
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Build a lightweight, repeatable pipeline and scoring model that surfaces 'latent' market signals (emergent open-model releases, quantization/format compatibility, latency-cost inflection points, vendor SLA changes, and regional capacity shocks) and produces a weekly prioritized list for model sourcing and fallback readiness. The intent is to reduce manual reconnaissance, give PMs and procurement a pro-active shortlist for trials, and create guardrails for rollout and Dedicated/Private procurement decisions. This work will combine automated scraping of public model manifests/GitHub releases, synthetic microbenchmarks (latency/cost by region), telemetry-derived usage patterns from a sample of customers, and structured competitive signals (pricing, API downtimes, quant recommendations).
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline ingests at least 5 distinct public signal sources (model releases, model manifests, GitHub tags, provider status pages, and cloud region latency probes) on a daily cadence

Scoring function implemented and documented that ranks models by combined score: availability risk, latency-cost arbitrage, quantization compatibility, and enterprise-fit (security/compliance indicators)
Weekly export: top-20 prioritized models with rationale, one-sentence trade-off summary, and suggested next-step (trial, trial+quant, or no-go)
Integrations: push summary rows to the procurement dashboard and create an alert when a high-risk supply shock is detected
Lightweight tech spec and runbook published (Confluence) describing data sources, scoring weights, and manual override process
tasks: Define initial signal taxonomy and weight heuristic with PM/R&D — due 2025-02-18
Implement scrapers/connectors for GitHub releases, model manifests, and provider status pages — infra spike 3d
Build microbenchmark harness (latency, memory, quant test) to run in 3 regions and report normalized metrics
Prototype scoring function and run curated seed models for validation
Add push to procurement dashboard and create alert rules for >30% capacity degradation or SLA change
Write Confluence spec and handoff to operations for maintenance
updates: 2025-02-13 — Kickoff: aligned on scope with PM, R&D, and Solutions. Decided to prioritize public signals first to avoid legal/contract friction.
2025-02-16 — Trade-off: finer-grained regional probes increase signal quality but cost 3x; agreed on a 3-region sampling baseline for MVP.
2025-02-20 — Tech review (R&D): recommended using existing benchmark harness from ENG-1842 to avoid duplicate work; assigned ENG-1842 as informal dependency.
2025-02-25 — UX/PM feedback: prefer simple human-readable rationale lines for each model rather than raw scores; updated acceptance criteria to include one-line trade-off summaries.
2025-03-01 — Data quality note: manifest formats vary; added normalization step and mapping doc (Confluence link) and scheduled follow-up to cover edge cases.

2025-03-05 — Status: scrapers 80% complete, microbenchmark infra deployed in us-west1/us-east1/europe-west1, initial scoring prototype running on seed list (25 models). Next: integrate output to procurement dashboard and finalize runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Signal noise from inconsistent manifest metadata — mitigation: require minimum fields and fall back to GitHub release timestamps and tag patterns
Cost of continuous microbenchmarks — mitigation: sample on a rolling window and opportunistically use customer shadow runs for deeper tests
False positives on availability alerts due to transient outages — mitigation: require 2x consecutive checks within 6h before firing high-severity procurement alerts
requested_reviews: Scoring function doc — review by Applied ML and Procurement
notes_for_followup: Validate scoring weights against historical model outage data (ask SRE for past 12 months incident logs)
Plan a 2-week field trial with Solutions Eng to run prioritized trials for top-5 models
Schedule 30m sync with Procurement and Legal before expanding to provider-specific pricing ingestion
